newsitem.title: UK: Emery sees 1997 E.European growth, expansion.
newsitem.headline: Emery sees 1997 E.European growth, expansion.

text.p: Emery Worldwide's Eastern and Central European division expects a 1997 turnover of more than $20 million, its general manager, Steve Soukup told Reuters.
"We're positioning very well for 1997. January, generally a quiet month, has already started the year on a very strong note," he said in a telephone interview from Zurich.
Soukup declined to give a precise revenue figure for last year but said: "1996 has been very good for us, developments were very positive last year."

Asked about this year's prospects for the different East and Central markets, Soukup said: "We're looking at some of these very closely. The whole area is under scrutiny and we have plans to expand our presence."
The company uses agents in some countries and "all options are being studied and explored", he said. These include agents, joint ventures or even opening direct offices.
The company's first East European office, opened in Budapest in June 1996, was "quite remarkable in becoming profitable in its first six months," he added.
Although end-year figures were not available, revenues from Hungary in the January-November period last year were 400 percent up on the same 1995 period with tonnages up 437 percent.
"Increased volumes certainly helped to achieve a profit at this stage in the operation with much of the increase coming in the second-half," Soukup said.

Revenues from Poland were 120 percent up on the same 1995 period, with tonnage up 140 percent; Austria recorded revenues up 150 percent with tonnage up 180 percent. Russia saw a 253 percent gain in revenue but no tonnage was available.
"We're also happy with the results from the Czech Republic and Switzerland (part of the division)," Soukup added without giving detailed figures.

The top product areas for the division are the automotive industry, fashion and textiles, aerospace -- especially in Russia,telecommunications including switching and paging equipment, medical and hospital equipment together with construction and energy equipment, he said.
